subject: Vulnerability remediation action matrix + scan cadence evidence request
messages:
From: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acmefin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: SecOps Team <security@acmefin.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VM cadence + proof for SOC2 audit

Hi Jonas,

We kicked off our SOC 2 readiness review and the auditor asked for more granular vulnerability management evidence from vendors with access to customer data. Specifically they want: a compact mapping that shows your recurring scan cadence (internal & third-party), SLA targets by CVE severity, a short sample of closure logs proving triage->patch->verify for a recent high/critical, and a summary of compensating controls where a patch was not possible.

Can you provide a single packet (PDF/CSV/Excel) that we can attach to the auditor folder? Our deadline to upload vendor evidence is next Wednesday, 23 May.

Thanks,
Audrey Chen
Security Program Manager
Acme Financial

[Note: auditor contact is Marco Ruiz at Auditeasy (marco.ruiz@auditeasy.com) who may reach out for clarifications.]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acmefin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence + proof for SOC2 audit

Hi Audrey — thanks for the heads up and the deadline. We can assemble a compact packet for the auditor. High level commitments we will include: 1) scan cadence matrix (weekly authenticated internal scans + biweekly external scans + monthly agent inventory sweep), 2) SLA targets: 72-hour initial triage for Critical, 7-day mitigation goal for High (hotfix or mitigations), 30-day target for Medium, 90-day for Low where compensating control applied, 3) a three-item closure sample (redacted) showing triage, assignment, remediation, and verification timestamps, and 4) a short explanation of exceptions/compensating controls and our rollback playbook.

We have an internal worksheet we'll export and attach — aiming to get the packet to you by Monday EOD so you have time to drop into the auditor folder.

Couple quick Qs so we meet auditor expectations: do they prefer a single archived ZIP or separate files uploaded to the shared drive? Also, are they okay with redacted hostnames if we remove customer-identifying data?

I'll assemble the packet and loop Ben for any billing-related exceptions the auditor flags.

—Jonas
VP, Customer Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acmefin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: SecOps Team <security@acmefin.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@auditeasy.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence + proof for SOC2 audit

Thanks Jonas — ZIP is preferred so the auditor has a single entry. Redacted hostnames are fine as long as timestamps and CVE IDs remain intact. Marco (auditor) — fyi, we'll accept redacted artifacts.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Audrey

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acmefin.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Deliverable: VM action matrix + sample closure logs (Redwood)

Hi Audrey & Marco — attaching the packet per the requested ZIP (attachment names below). Highlights included in the packet: a one-page cadence summary (scan-cadence-summary-2028Q2.pdf), an actionable CVE matrix (rdi_vuln_action_matrix_20280516.xlsx) that maps severity->SLA->owner->mitigation type, and a sample closure log export (cve-closure-log-snippet.csv) with three recently closed issues (one Critical* marked as router-facing kernel CVE — redacted). We also included a short note describing compensating controls for one item we couldn't patch immediately (WAF rule + host isolation).

Key clarifications:
- Our priority timeline: initial triage within 72 hours of detection for Criticals; Criticals are escalated to a hotpatch committee if the patch path is nontrivial.
- Where a vendor patch is unavailable we document mitigations and set a reviewer cadence every 7 days until a patch is applied.
- Verification includes a follow-up authenticated scan plus internal QA sign-off.

Attachments (in ZIP): rdi_vuln_action_matrix_20280516.xlsx (action matrix), scan-cadence-summary-2028Q2.pdf (one-pager), cve-closure-log-snippet.csv (redacted sample).

Ben — I flagged three items for potential billing credits for extended remediations; will work with you on any customer asks.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: rdi_vuln_action_matrix_20280516.xlsx (xlsx), scan-cadence-summary-2028Q2.pdf (pdf), cve-closure-log-snippet.csv (csv)]

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@auditeasy.com>
To: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acmefin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deliverable: VM action matrix + sample closure logs (Redwood)

Marissa / Jonas — received and reviewed the ZIP. Packet looks clear and audit-ready. A couple of minor asks: please confirm timestamp timezone for the closure CSV (we saw PST vs UTC entries) and provide a short statement we can attach that declares the SLAs are applicable to Redwood-hosted production services (not third-party sandbox environments). If you can provide those two one-liners as a signed text file, we can include them verbatim in the SOC 2 vendor evidence appendix.

If you can drop that small file in the shared folder by EOD tomorrow, we can finalize the vendor packet.

Regards,
Marco Ruiz
Lead Auditor, Auditeasy

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@auditeasy.com>, Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acmefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deliverable: VM action matrix + sample closure logs (Redwood)

Marco — thanks for the quick review. Quick confirmations below (we will also upload a signed TXT):
1) All timestamps in cve-closure-log-snippet.csv are in UTC; the file header had an internal export tag that showed PST — we corrected the header and will include the corrected CSV in the ZIP.
2) Statement for auditor: "Redwood Inference confirms the VM cadence and SLA commitments described in the attached action matrix are applicable to Redwood-managed production services that handle customer data. Sandbox and partner test environments follow separate dev/test cadence and are excluded from these SLA targets."

We'll upload the corrected CSV and the signed TXT (GPG-signed by security@redwood.com) to the shared folder by EOD. Let me know if you need anything else.

—Jonas
VP, Customer Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference
